1.name: Dual-Shift
1.description: Both hands shift (move to adjacent grid points). This is the most common letter type.
characteristics: Both hands move 90 degrees on the grid
Creates smooth, flowing transitions
22 letters - the largest type
Organized by VTG timing+direction: Split-Same (ABC), Together-Opp (DEF), Together-Same (GHI), Split-Opp (JKL), Quarter-Opp (M-R), Quarter-Same (STUV)
Each group is pro + anti + hybrid = 3 letters, except Quarter-Same, which has 4
Quarter-Same's hybrid splits into U (leader pro) and V (leader anti) because same-direction shifts at a right angle have a leader and follower. Quarter-Opposite (M-R) has no leader/follower

2.name: Shift
2.description: One hand shifts while the other stays static. Creates asymmetric movements.
characteristics: One hand moves, one stays in place
Often used for transitions between symmetric and asymmetric placements
Uses Greek letters for most of this type

motionPattern.note: Exactly one hand shifts, one is static

3.name: Cross-Shift
3.description: One hand shifts and one hand dashes. Also called 'dash letters' due to the '-' suffix in their names.
characteristics: Combines shift (90 degree) and dash (180 degree) motions
Named with a '-' suffix (e.g., 'W-', 'Sigma-')
IMPORTANT: 'Sigma dash' means the letter Sigma- (Type 3), not a letter with dash motion

4.name: Dash
4.description: One hand follows the dash hand-path family while the other stays static.
characteristics: Creates dramatic placement changes
Uses Greek letters Phi, Psi, Lambda
3 Level 1 letters, plus the Level 6 Tau-Dash extension
Phi = diverging (angular separation increases): beta→alpha, or eta→zeta on 8-point grid
Psi = converging (angular separation decreases): alpha→beta, or zeta→eta on 8-point grid
Lambda = angle preserved (gamma→gamma). Cannot be skewed (gamma requires both hands on same grid)

motionPattern.note: Exactly one hand dashes, one is static

5.name: Dual-Dash
5.description: Both hands dash simultaneously (both move to opposite points).
characteristics: Both hands move 180 degrees
Creates dramatic, symmetric movements
Named with '-' suffix like Type 3
Only 3 letters in this type
Same diverge/converge/preserve pattern as Type 4. Lambda- cannot be skewed (same reason as Lambda)

6.name: Static
6.description: Both hands remain stationary. The props may still rotate, but hands don't change placement.
characteristics: No hand movement
Focus is entirely on prop rotation
Uses lowercase Greek letters
Good for 'breathing space' in sequences
